agent_profile.assumption: The agent has useful but limited reasoning capacity and must not be treated as a reliable global repository reasoner.
agent_profile.design_consequence: Tasks, evidence, decisions, and output schemas must be narrowly bounded.

core_design_rule.statement: No agent invocation may be responsible for understanding or validating the repository as a whole.
core_design_rule.implementation: Repository-wide validation is produced by deterministic composition of many small regime results.
core_design_rule.authority_owner: explicit departmental policy and operator-approved governance

agent_capability_limits.response: Provide only the files, excerpts, schemas, rules, and dependency summaries required for the current task.

agent_capability_limits.limit: Weak global reconciliation across many documents
agent_capability_limits.response: Use separate extraction, comparison, and disposition tasks rather than one combined reasoning task.

agent_capability_limits.limit: Susceptibility to confident inference from incomplete evidence
agent_capability_limits.response: Require evidence references for every finding and provide an explicit INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE result.

agent_capability_limits.limit: Potential inconsistency across long or repeated workflows
agent_capability_limits.response: Use immutable task packets, stable identifiers, enums, and deterministic result validation.

agent_capability_limits.limit: Difficulty distinguishing current authority from historical material
agent_capability_limits.response: Resolve authority and supersession before presenting evidence to the worker.

agent_capability_limits.limit: Difficulty applying many interacting policies simultaneously
agent_capability_limits.response: Each regime task may apply only a small declared rule set.
Provide an explicit checklist of required checks and require a result for every checklist item.
Completeness must be calculated mechanically from required check identifiers.

department_architecture.principle: Hierarchical decomposition without hierarchical free-form reasoning

responsibilities: reduce atomic results into regime status

layers.owner: bounded comparison workers plus deterministic conflict detection
responsibilities: compare two or three regime facts
accept closure of recurrent defect classes

task_size_constraints.task_packet_rule: If a task exceeds any limit, it must be divided before agent execution.
task_size_constraints.exception_rule: Exceptions require an explicit operator-approved task profile and may not become the default.

forbidden_task_language: infer the current source of truth
task_packet_requirements.required_task_language_pattern: Inspect the listed inputs for the listed conditions and return only the allowed result types.

worker_must: cite an exact evidence location for every non-pass result
return INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when the supplied packet cannot support a decision
worker_must_not: interpret absent evidence as evidence of absence
edit files unless assigned a separate repair task

required_shape.status: PASS | FAIL | WARNING | NOT_APPLICABLE | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | EXECUTION_ERROR

evidence.location: line, object key, symbol, command output, or hash

mechanical_acceptance_rules: Every required check_id must appear exactly once.
Every FAIL or WARNING must contain evidence.
A PASS may not contain unresolved questions affecting that check.
The result is rejected if scope_expansion_requested is true.
The result is rejected if an unknown status is used.
The agent's overall status is advisory until deterministically reduced.

regime_must_not: interpret another regime's evidence without a comparison task
use free-form prose as its authoritative result

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Test discovery and collection
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Does the canonical test command collect the declared test surface without error?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Test execution results
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Did every collected test complete with an allowed outcome?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Environment reproducibility
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Does the active environment match the declared dependency and runtime manifest?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Tracked repository composition
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Do tracked files comply with the declared repository retention and hygiene rules?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Document authority and supersession
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Does each governed document class have one declared current authority?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Cross-document factual synchronization
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Do selected paired documents agree on the listed facts?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Evidence structure
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Does each evidence artifact satisfy its declared schema and required fields?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Evidence origin and traceability
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Can each evidence artifact be traced to declared inputs, execution, and producing version?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Synthetic and mock evidence isolation
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Can synthetic outputs be mechanically distinguished from admissible evidence?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Governance record integrity
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Do governance records satisfy required identifiers, transitions, references, and authority rules?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Declared formal-system components
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Are the specifically required formal components present and explicitly defined?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Claim language versus registered evidence
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Does each selected claim remain within its registered evidence classification?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Input change after validation
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Have authoritative inputs changed since the regime result was produced?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Historical supersession
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Has a newer authoritative artifact explicitly superseded the selected artifact?

initial_regime_catalog.subject: Finding recurrence
initial_regime_catalog.bounded_question: Does the current defect match the identity or failure class of a previously closed finding?

staleness_department_design.principle: Staleness is not one model judgment.

staleness_dimensions.determination: hash or version changed after validation
upstream regime or evidence was invalidated
artifact remains present but its statements conflict with current authority
historical finding no longer reproduces and its failure path is protected
a previously closed failure class has recurred

staleness_department_design.mini_agent_rule: A single task may evaluate only one staleness dimension for one artifact or one small artifact group.

finding_memory.purpose: Prevent Codex Mini from reconstructing issue history from scattered prose.

record_schema.title: short title
record_schema.current_disposition: OPEN | FIX_PENDING | FIXED_UNVERIFIED | FIXED_VERIFIED | STALE_SUPERSEDED | RECURRENT | ACCEPTED_DEBT | INVALID_FINDING

finding_memory.agent_use: Workers receive the relevant finding record directly and must not search historical reports unless assigned a separate history-extraction task.

repair_workflow.separation_rule: Validation tasks detect and classify. Repair tasks modify. Verification tasks test the repair. No single invocation performs all three.
repair_workflow.closure_rule: Codex Mini may recommend closure but may not independently close a recurrent failure class.

prompt_style: no requirement to remember earlier conversations

departmental_output_rule.statement: The departmental report is assembled from validated regime records, not written by a model from raw repository evidence.
allowed_model_contribution: bounded summaries of already validated regime facts
repair recommendations tied to registered findings

success_condition.statement: The Validation Department succeeds when a weaker model can reliably execute every assigned task because the architecture has removed the need for broad implicit reasoning.
measures: average evidence set size per task
